pr_title: Fix explain and hybrid search scoring bug
pr_body:
This PR addresses bugs with KNN search.

First, when searching with KNN, using `explain: true` would give strange results. 

Even though a document obviously matches because of its score, the explanation would indicate that it did NOT match. This bug was because our explanation check was not accounting for the leaf-segment's docBase.

Second, when there are multiple segments, and KNN is used in hybrid search, some documents may go unscored by KNN.

The main issue here is the disjunction logic within `BoolQuery`. All hybrid queries with `knn` are pure disjunction queries under the hood. And Lucene does its best to optimize the documents it gathers in these types of queries.

Consequently, it will look for the maximum possible score for an entire segment leaf. However, the underlying KNN query would ALWAYS increment this passed docId by the segment's docBase (this is fairly ironic given the `explain` bug :D). This would cause the `docId` for calculating the maximum score to roll over to the negatives and thus knn would indicate its maximum score to be `0` for certain segments with higher docBase values.

closes: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/93830
pr_comments: Hi @benwtrent, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
Big thanks to @xiankgx for providing the initial bug report here!

> Also, we need tests for explain with multiple segments?

The test I have does that. The flushing periodically allows for multiple segments to be created.

issue_context.title: Vector search hybrid score surprising behavior
issue_context.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

8.x

### Installed Plugins

_No response_

### Java Version

any

### OS Version

any

### Problem Description

When searching over multiple vectors, when `k` and `size` are the same, hybrid search produces strange results.

Here is an example from explain

```
"_explanation": {
                    "value": 1.6323383,
                    "description": "sum of:",
                    "details": [
                        {
                            "value": 1,
                            "description": "ConstantScore(*:*)",
                            "details": []
                        }
                    ]
                }
```

Obviously, the score is augmented by `knn`, but here it indicates it isn't. 

And here:
```
                "_explanation": {
                    "value": 1,
                    "description": "sum of:",
                    "details": [
                        {
                            "value": 1,
                            "description": "ConstantScore(*:*)",
                            "details": []
                        }
                    ]
                }
```

The document in question HAS vectors and its score SHOULD be augmented by knn, but instead the vector score is not present at all.


### Steps to Reproduce

See: https://github.com/xiankgx/es-debug

### Logs (if relevant)

_No response_

review_comments: `doc` here is always the doc related to the context base. So, we need to add the base.

Previously, this was getting the max score across ALL previous segments and the current one. This seemed weird to me. We should only return the max for the given segment, correct?

@jpountz am I correct on this?
This is the other bug fix. When `NO_MORE_DOCS` is passed, it means we gather the max doc to the END of the given segment.

We can optimize our `count` since `segmentStarts` indicate the number of documents within that segment. So, count can be constant time. This is a minor optimization, but prevents creating a scorer and iterating docs needlessly.
I think it would be wise to make this change separately. it's a good one but it's a performance improvement rather than a bugfix.
